question: Which statement best describes aspect-ratio?
options: `aspect-ratio` describes the width-to-height relationship of a box, such as `16 / 9`. The browser can reserve that shape before an image finishes loading, which reduces layout jumps. It is like choosing a picture frame before printing the photo. Apply it to a media wrapper and check it at narrow widths.

`object-position` moves the visible part of an image when the box crops it. For example, `object-position: center top` keeps more of the upper area in view. It is like sliding a photo behind a fixed window. Choose a focal point that keeps useful context visible.

`object-fit: contain` keeps the full image visible inside its box, though empty space may remain around it. It is like shrinking a poster to fit a frame without cutting its text. Use it for product diagrams, logos, and screenshots where every edge matters.

`object-fit: cover` fills the image box while keeping the source proportions, so some edges may be cropped. It is like trimming a photo to fill a frame. This works for uniform thumbnails, but inspect the crop so a face, label, or important object is not cut off.
explanation: `aspect-ratio` describes the width-to-height relationship of a box, such as `16 / 9`. The browser can reserve that shape before an image finishes loading, which reduces layout jumps. It is like choosing a picture frame before printing the photo. Apply it to a media wrapper and check it at narrow widths.
